subject: mathematics
question_text: If f: R → R is defined by f(x) = (1 − x²)/(1 + x²), show that f(tan θ) = cos 2θ.

recall_prompt: Say how you would show f(tan θ) = cos 2θ — what you substitute, and how you clear the tangents.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Put x = tan θ in the rule
steps.margin_note: First mark is the substituted fraction. Also say where tan θ exists: θ must not be an odd multiple of π/2.
steps.memory_tip: f(anything) means put that thing where x stands. Here every x becomes tan θ.
lines: Put x = tan θ, taking θ so that tan θ exists,

recall.must_convey: That f(tan θ) is the same rule with tan θ in place of x, giving (1 − tan²θ)/(1 + tan²θ).
accept: put tan theta where x is so it becomes one minus tan squared over one plus tan squared
substitute x equals tan theta into the given rule
f of tan theta is one minus tan square theta by one plus tan square theta
x place lo tan theta pedithe one minus tan square by one plus tan square vasthundi
replace x by tan theta in the fraction

steps.why: f is given by a rule in x, so f(tan θ) is that rule with tan θ written wherever x appeared. Nothing else about f changes. The one condition to state is that tan θ must exist, so θ is not an odd multiple of π/2.
common_mistakes: Reading f(tan θ) as tan of f(θ).
Writing (tan θ)² as tan θ², which is the tangent of θ².

steps.label: Clear the tangents and reach cos 2θ
steps.margin_note: Second mark is the reduction. Check with θ = 30°: tan 30° = 1/√3, so f = (1 − 1/3)/(1 + 1/3) = 1/2, and cos 60° = 1/2.
steps.memory_tip: Multiply the top and the bottom by cos²θ. The bottom becomes 1 and the top becomes cos²θ − sin²θ, which is cos 2θ.
lines: Write tan θ = sin θ/cos θ, then multiply the
numerator and the denominator by cos²θ:

recall.must_convey: That multiplying the top and bottom by cos²θ gives (cos²θ − sin²θ)/1, which is cos 2θ.
accept: multiply top and bottom by cos squared theta so the bottom becomes one
the numerator becomes cos square minus sin square which is cos two theta
cos square plus sin square is one so only the numerator is left
cos square theta tho multiply chesthe denominator one authundi
it reduces to cos square minus sin square theta equals cos two theta

steps.why: Multiplying the top and the bottom by cos²θ clears every tangent at once. The denominator becomes cos²θ + sin²θ, which is 1, and the numerator becomes cos²θ − sin²θ, which is the double angle form of cos 2θ.
common_mistakes: Multiplying only the numerator by cos²θ.
Writing cos²θ + sin²θ as 2 instead of 1.
